content:
- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Overshoots after sharp upward spikes in history (e.g., after 66.63→68.27, model jumps to 69+).
- Underestimates in late horizon (last 5–10 days), particularly when true values rise sharply (e.g., 68.27→73.00).
- Shows persistent lag in capturing true trend reversals — model reacts slower to downward momentum.
- Mean reversion bias: model assumes prices will return to prior mean too quickly, underestimating volatility in late horizon.
- Horizon-specific: first 10 days often overestimated, last 10 days underestimated — model fails to adjust for tail risk or policy-driven volatility.
